item.title: AkzoNobel to sell unit to Nippon Paint for over $1 billion, FT reports
item.description: Dulux paint maker AkzoNobel is nearing a deal to sell its Southeast Asian decorative paints business to Nippon Paint for well over $1 billion, the Financial Times reported on Sunday, citing people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Dulux paint maker AkzoNobel (AKZO.AS) is nearing a deal to sell its Southeast Asian decorative paints business to Nippon Paint (4612.T) for well over $1 billion, the Financial Times reported on Sunday, citing people familiar with the matter. The Dutch company could reach an agreement as early as Monday, the newspaper said. The divestment would include decorative paint operations in Vietnam, Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand and Singapore, as well as Papua New Guinea and Australia. Reuters could not immediately verify the FT report. AkzoNobel and Nippon Paint did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment. Nippon Paint submitted [USN:L6N43F003 TEXT:"multiple proposals"] to acquire AkzoNobel's decorative paints business, AkzoNobel said in July, valuing it at about €7.5 billion ($8.44 billion). That approach followed the [USN:L6N42B0EM TEXT:"withdrawal"] of a €12.5 billion bid for the entire company that Nippon Paint had pursued jointly with US-based paintmaker Sherwin-Williams (SHW.N) in June. The FT report added that Nippon remains interested in a larger deal for the decorative paint business, but that integration of the Southeast Asia business could occupy the company for some time and that AkzoNobel does not have plans to sell further assets from the business. ($1 = 0.8887 euros)

item.title: Manchester City beat hapless Arsenal 4-2 to stay top of WSL
item.description: Lauren Hemp scored twice as Manchester City came from behind on two occasions to beat Arsenal 4-2 in the Women's Super League on Sunday, keeping the champions top of the table heading into the international break after a fifth straight win from their opening five matches.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Lauren Hemp scored twice as Manchester City came from behind on two occasions to beat Arsenal 4-2 in the Women's Super League on Sunday, keeping the champions top of the table heading into the international break after a fifth straight win from their opening five matches. Arsenal went ahead through Lisa Baum in the 43rd minute, but City levelled when Hemp forced the ball home from a tight angle in first-half stoppage time. Alessia Russo put the Gunners back in front four minutes after the break but again City came back, Kerstin Casparij equalising in the 63rd minute before Hemp put them in front for the first time nine minutes later. Striker Bunny Shaw sealed the three points in the 84th minute with her fifth goal of the season to condemn Arsenal, who are without a win since the opening day of the season, to their second straight defeat after losing 1-0 away to Chelsea last week. The loss leaves Arsenal in 10th spot on five points from five games after a dismal start to the campaign. Earlier in the afternoon, Sonia Bompastor's Chelsea thumped West Ham United 3-0 to put them into second place, two points behind City. They took the lead thanks to a Melvine Malard strike and added two late goals through Keira Walsh and Maika Hamano. London City Lionesses showed that they will be a force to be reckoned with in the title race, Alexia Putellas scoring twice in the first half of a 6-1 thrashing of Tottenham Hotspur, who were left shell-shocked by the pressing of the visitors. Spurs had only conceded two goals in the first four outings, but they were hit for six as London City notched their third successive win in impressive fashion to move to third place on 12 points. Charlton Athletic, who are still searching for their first point since being promoted, remain bottom of the 14-team table after a 5-1 hammering at the hands of Brighton & Hove Albion, with Kiko Seike scoring twice for the Seagulls. Everton's strong start to the season continued with a 2-1 win over Birmingham City that lifts them to fifth spot in the table on nine points, two ahead of cross-town rivals Liverpool, who lost 1-0 to Manchester United on Saturday.

item.title: South Africa's Nortje eyes test return against Australia after lengthy absence
item.description: South Africa fast bowler Anrich Nortje could make a remarkable return to first-class cricket after an absence of almost four years to help an injury-hampered South Africa attack in the first test against Australia, which starts in Durban on Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: South Africa fast bowler Anrich Nortje could make a remarkable return to first-class cricket after an absence of almost four years to help an injury-hampered South Africa attack in the first test against Australia, which starts in Durban on Friday. With fitness doubts over pace spearhead Kagiso Rabada and three other bowlers ruled out with hamstring injuries, Nortje is set to return to red-ball cricket for the first time since South Africa's test victory over West Indies in March 2023. That match, in which he took 5-36 in the first innings, was Nortje's last first-class appearance. A succession of injury setbacks, as he struggled with back and hip problems, subsequently led him to focus on the shorter formats, where bowling in brief spells has helped reduce the strain on his body. The 32-year-old has evolved into a T20 specialist, but said on Sunday he had been working on his red-ball skills. "It's been quite a bit of a focus for me to try and execute skills with the red ball, to build loads gradually and in the right way try and get the overs up,” he told reporters on Sunday. “It's something that I've been doing for quite some time. There's been quite some effort put in to try and upskill again, and improve from where I left off. "I'll be very excited if I can put my test cap on again. Growing up, it's the format you want to play. It's the motivation when you train," he added. Nortje has featured in 19 tests with a bowling average of 26.71 and regularly bowled at speeds in excess of 145kph – with his action taking a heavy toll on his body. TEST CRICKET BRINGS OUT EXTRA FIRE "You don't think of the tough times in T20 cricket. You just think about executing skills there, whereas in tests, you think about the tough times, the good times, the hard work and think that gets you through some sessions. "There's just that little bit of extra X-factor that comes out, or fire that comes out, and energy that comes out," Nortje added. "Guys want to do well, and everyone wants to perform. It is a big series." South Africa started an intra-squad match on Sunday and late Monday will cut their preliminary squad from 18 to 15, with Nortje expected to make the cut despite his lengthy absence. "The guys have grown quite a bit,” he said of the test side which has since gone on to win the World Test Championship, beating Australia in mid-2025. “They've played a lot and they've done really well. Hopefully, I can just add on to that. I'm very keen to get going and be on the park and try to do well for the country," Nortje added.

item.title: Valkyries' Janelle Salaun unanimous choice as Sixth Player of Year
item.description: Golden State Valkyries forward Janelle Salaun was unanimously selected as the 2026 WNBA Sixth Player of the Year, the league announced Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Golden State Valkyries forward Janelle Salaun was unanimously selected as the 2026 WNBA Sixth Player of the Year, the league announced Sunday. Salaun earned the honor for the first time after receiving all 74 votes from a national panel of sportswriters and broadcasters. A player had to play more games as a reserve than as a starter to be eligible for the award. Salaun, 25, led all WNBA reserves in scoring with 12.7 points per game. The 6-foot-2 France native came off the bench in all 40 of the games in which she played, setting league single-season records for points (509) and 3-pointers made (93) by a reserve. Naz Hillmon of the Atlanta Dream won the award last year. --Field Level Media

item.title: Eagles RB Saquon Barkley out vs. Rams with hamstring injury
item.description: Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley was ruled out of Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Rams after he sustained a hamstring injury on his second carry.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley was ruled out of Sunday's game against the Los Angeles Rams after he sustained a hamstring injury on his second carry. Barkley was limping on the sideline at the end of a 6-yard run with 11:34 left in the first quarter. Replays showed him rubbing the back of his right leg before going to the medical tent. He was replaced by Tank Bigsby before heading to the locker room. The team initially said he was questionable to return. Barkley, 29, has rushed for 182 yards and no touchdowns in four games this season, including 8 yards on his two carries Sunday. In his previous three games against the Rams since joining Philadelphia, Barkley rushed for 506 yards and four touchdowns on 70 carries. That included a franchise-record 255-yard game on Nov. 24, 2024 and a team playoff-record 205 yards in a divisional round game on Jan. 19, 2025. The Philadelphia offense already was playing without top wide receiver DeVonta Smith (hamstring), tight end Dallas Goedert (knee) and right tackle Lane Johnson (personal). --Field Level Media

item.title: Colorado State DC out after mid-game demotion
item.description: The in-game decision by Colorado State head coach Jim Mora on Saturday to change defensive play-callers led to the dismissal of the Rams' defensive coordinator.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The in-game decision by Colorado State head coach Jim Mora on Saturday to change defensive play-callers led to the dismissal of the Rams' defensive coordinator. As he watched Oregon State pile up the yards in an eventual 56-26 loss, Mora told defensive coordinator Tyson Summers that he was done calling plays for the day. Mora transferred the duties to associate head coach and defensive line coach Kenny McClendon. When Summers departed the field after his demotion, that ended his tenure at Colorado State. "Tyson was relieved of his play-calling duties. He left the field, and he is no longer with this football program," Mora said postgame. "That is permanent." The change occurred in the first half, per local reports. At halftime, the Beavers had a 35-14 lead. Oregon State finished with 650 yards of total offense -- 223 on the ground and 427 via air as Beavers quarterback Braden Atkinson finished the game 31-of-34 passing with five touchdowns. Summers, 46, has an extensive coaching background, beginning in the college ranks at his alma mater - Presbyterian - in 2003. He got his first chance as a defensive coordinator at UCF (2012-14), followed by a season as DC and safeties coach at Colorado State, departing for a two-year stint as head coach at Georgia Southern. Summers also spent two seasons as the DC at Colorado (2019-20), then three at Western Kentucky in the same role (2022-24) before returning to Colorado State in 2025 as DC under Jay Norvell. When Norvell was fired seven games into last season, Summers took over as interim coach, and the Rams finished with an 0-5 record. Colorado State (2-3), which has not finished above .500 since 2017, snatched Mora last fall from UConn, where he rebuilt the struggling program in four seasons. Previously the head coach at UCLA and in the NFL with the Atlanta Falcons and Seattle Seahawks, Mora kept Summers on board. Mora, 64, said McClendon will be the defensive coordinator for the rest of the season. "He was put in a very difficult situation, and he responded well, the players responded well," Mora said. "Very first play he called as a defensive coordinator in his entire life was a sack, caused a fumble. So we're going to get better, we're going to get a lot better. He's a good football coach." Colorado State defeated Wyoming and Southern Utah to start the season, allowing 37 total points. Since then, in losses to BYU, UTSA and Oregon State, the Rams have surrendered 156 points -- an average of 52 per game. --Field Level Media

item.title: Nunes Marques diz esperar judicialização das eleições, mas afirma que pleito transcorre normalmente
item.description: O presidente do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), Kassio Nunes Marques, afirmou neste domingo ser esperado que candidatos acionem a Justiça com questionamentos relacionados às eleições, mas ponderou que a votação está transcorrendo com normalidade e transparência, também sem indícios de interferência internacional.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O presidente do Tribunal Superior Eleitoral (TSE), Kassio Nunes Marques, afirmou neste domingo ser esperado que candidatos acionem a Justiça com questionamentos relacionados às eleições, mas ponderou que a votação está transcorrendo com normalidade e transparência, também sem indícios de interferência internacional. Em entrevista coletiva por volta das 14h com dados preliminares sobre a eleição, Nunes Marques afirmou que as urnas estão funcionando normalmente e não houve necessidade de uso de votação manual em nenhum ponto do país. “Há uma tradição na justiça brasileira de judicialização, então seria de se esperar que os candidatos, não só à Presidência da República, mas deputados estaduais e federais e governadores batam às portas da Justiça com os seus questionamentos”, disse, citando como exemplos ações sobre abuso de poder político e econômico de candidatos. “Estamos bastante confiantes de que até agora não temos ainda do que se queixar", disse Nunes Marques. "Tudo tem funcionado na maior normalidade e com a maior transparência possível.” De acordo com o presidente do TSE, 1.121 urnas com algum tipo de falha foram substituídas, 0,2% do total. Em relação a irregularidades, Nunes Marques afirmou que 59 pessoas foram conduzidas pela polícia por suspeita de crime eleitoral e mais de R$380 mil em espécie foram apreendidos. Ele enfatizou que o TSE não identificou nenhum indicativo de interferência estrangeira nas eleições. “Equipes que monitoram riscos internacionais não apontam qualquer tipo de risco”, afirmou. O diretor-geral da Polícia Federal, Andrei Rodrigues, afirmou mais cedo neste domingo que a corporação abriu [USN:L1N45Q03S TEXT:"investigação"] para apurar suposto esquema de financiamento de uma agenda de extrema-direita no Brasil pelo governo norte-americano de Donald Trump que teria entre os objetivos interferir nas eleições brasileiras. A investigação foi solicitada pela Advocacia-Geral da União (AGU).

item.title: Australia investiga los vínculos del copiloto de flydubai con el país, dice la policía
item.description: Una unidad antiterrorista australiana en la que participan varios organismos está investigando los vínculos con Australia del copiloto del vuelo FZ1073 de flydubai, quien apuñaló a su capitán y luego intentó secuestrar el avión, informó el domingo un portavoz de la policía.
item.dc:creator: Praveen Menon, Alexander Cornwell
item.content:encoded: Una unidad antiterrorista australiana en la que participan varios organismos está investigando los vínculos con Australia del copiloto del vuelo FZ1073 de flydubai, quien apuñaló a su capitán y luego intentó secuestrar el avión, informó el domingo un portavoz de la policía. El Equipo Conjunto Antiterrorista de Victoria, integrado por la policía federal, la policía estatal de Victoria y la agencia de inteligencia ASIO, estaba "investigando los vínculos de este hombre con Australia", dijo el portavoz de la Policía Federal Australiana. Dos fuentes al tanto de la investigación indicaron que el copiloto estudió en una universidad de Melbourne, la capital del estado australiano de Victoria. Una tercera fuente señaló que estudió en la Universidad RMIT hace aproximadamente una década. La RMIT declinó hacer comentarios. El copiloto del vuelo FZ1073 de flydubai, que el miércoles se dirigía a Israel desde Dubái, atacó al piloto con un hacha de emergencia, según dijo el sábado el fiscal general de los Emiratos Árabes Unidos, que calificó el incidente de "ataque terrorista". El vuelo FZ1073 debió de parecer una "montaña rusa vertical", ya que descendió 16.000 pies en unos 30 segundos antes de estabilizarse y aterrizar sin incidentes, según un instructor de aviación que recreó el descenso en un simulador de vuelo para Reuters. COPILOTO DETENIDO EN LOS EAU Dos fuentes han afirmado que el copiloto es un ciudadano omaní llamado Hamam Al-Hamami. Las autoridades israelíes no han revelado el nombre del copiloto, pero han indicado que es de Omán. Las autoridades de los EAU y flydubai no han hecho pública la identidad del copiloto. Reuters no ha podido contactar de forma independiente con Al-Hamami, que se encuentra bajo custodia en los Emiratos Árabes Unidos, para recabar sus comentarios. Los Emiratos Árabes Unidos no han anunciado ningún cargo formal contra él y se desconoce si ha designado a un abogado. Omán no se ha pronunciado sobre el incidente. Se evitó una catástrofe a bordo del vuelo FZ1073 después de que los pasajeros y la tripulación redujeran al copiloto, quien había atacado al capitán en lo que, según las autoridades israelíes, fue un intento de estrellar el avión, que transportaba a más de 170 pasajeros y tripulantes. El fiscal general de los Emiratos Árabes Unidos ha declarado que el copiloto había intentado tomar el control del avión. La mayoría de los pasajeros a bordo eran ciudadanos israelíes. Un piloto de reserva de flydubai que viajaba en ese vuelo tomó el control de la aeronave y la hizo aterrizar en el aeropuerto de Tabuk, en el noroeste de Arabia Saudita, donde el copiloto fue detenido por las autoridades sauditas y posteriormente trasladado a los Emiratos Árabes Unidos el jueves. El Financial Times informó el domingo de que Al-Hamami habría visitado lo que describió como mezquitas radicales y páginas web extremistas durante su estancia en Australia, citando a dos personas familiarizadas con la investigación. Según el Financial Times, los servicios de inteligencia australianos tenían un expediente sobre esta persona. Reuters no pudo verificar de inmediato la información del FT. El Gobierno de Australia no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios fuera del horario laboral habitual. El primer ministro israelí, Benjamin Netanyahu, dijo que el copiloto había sido sometido a un adoctrinamiento islamista radical y que tenía claras intenciones suicidas, aunque no ha precisado cuándo ni dónde se produjo supuestamente dicho adoctrinamiento. El domingo ordenó al Consejo de Seguridad Nacional que nombrara a un investigador para "llevar a cabo una revisión exhaustiva de todos los aspectos de seguridad relacionados con la aviación civil extranjera con destino a Israel". Israel no mantiene relaciones diplomáticas oficiales con Omán, y Netanyahu también ha afirmado que no se permite a pilotos de esos países operar vuelos con destino a Israel. No está claro cómo llegó a ser asignado el copiloto al vuelo con destino a Tel Aviv.

item.title: Merz anuncia nuevas ayudas militares en Kiev y dice que Alemania no se dejará intimidar
item.description: Alemania no se dejará intimidar para que retire su apoyo a Ucrania, dijo el domingo el canciller Friedrich Merz, al anunciar una nueva ayuda militar de 1.000 millones de euros (1.100 millones de dólares) durante una visita a Kiev marcada por los ataques con drones rusos.
item.dc:creator: Andreas Rinke, Felix Hoske
item.content:encoded: Alemania no se dejará intimidar para que retire su apoyo a Ucrania, dijo el domingo el canciller Friedrich Merz, al anunciar una nueva ayuda militar de 1.000 millones de euros (1.100 millones de dólares) durante una visita a Kiev marcada por los ataques con drones rusos. Las sirenas antiaéreas y las explosiones resonaron repetidamente en toda la capital ucraniana mientras Merz y el presidente ucraniano, Volodímir Zelenski, visitaban un monumento en memoria de los soldados fallecidos durante la guerra, que ya dura cuatro años, así como la Academia de Ciencias, donde al menos dos personas murieron en un ataque con drones la semana pasada. Rusia ha intensificado sus ataques con drones contra Kiev y otras ciudades en las últimas semanas, apuntando a infraestructuras de telecomunicaciones, electricidad y transporte, así como contra instalaciones militares. En una rueda de prensa junto a Zelenski, Merz dijo que Moscú estaba intentando minar la confianza del pueblo ucraniano y anunció una ayuda de 350 millones de euros para las reparaciones en el sector energético. Afirmó que Alemania seguía siendo el principal aliado de Ucrania. "Hacemos esto no solo para proteger la integridad territorial de Ucrania; lo hacemos en nuestro propio interés, ya que es una cuestión de seguridad para Europa", dijo Merz, señalando que Rusia estaba llevando a cabo ciberataques y campañas de desinformación que atentaban contra el orden democrático europeo. "Esto demuestra que no nos dejaremos intimidar", añadió. Rusia ha afirmado que las acusaciones de guerra híbrida carecen de fundamento y son fruto de la histeria antirrusa. Las autoridades indicaron que los directivos de las empresas alemanas, que viajaron con Merz, habían firmado 16 acuerdos con el Gobierno y empresas ucranianas por un valor aproximado de 6.500 millones de euros. Entre esos acuerdos, Ucrania firmó un contrato con la firma alemana Diehl Defence para el suministro de misiles de defensa aérea IRIS-T, así como un acuerdo para equipos de radar con Hensoldt y para drones interceptores a reacción con Quantum Systems. Zelenski elogió un nuevo dron interceptor a reacción, denominado SPYS y desarrollado por Quantum, por mostrar resultados prometedores. Dijo que Ucrania y Alemania estaban a punto de cerrar un amplio acuerdo de defensa que, según había declarado anteriormente, incluiría la producción de drones, misiles y software relacionado. ZELENSKI SE COMPROMETE A RESPONDER Desde el verano boreal, Rusia ha atacado a diario infraestructuras civiles y militares con decenas de drones de ataque a reacción de alta velocidad, que Ucrania ha tenido dificultades para derribar debido a que son mucho más rápidos que las versiones anteriores con hélice. Uno de los ataques rusos del domingo alcanzó el Puente del Norte, que cruza el río Dniéper, dañando su calzada, según informó el alcalde de Kiev, Vitali Klitschko, a través de Telegram. La explosión dejó dos heridos y dañó un sistema de suministro de agua caliente de la zona, añadió. Zelenski dijo que la decisión de Rusia de intensificar los ataques aéreos contra objetivos de infraestructura se debía a los reveses que había sufrido en el campo de batalla, y prometió que Ucrania tomaría represalias. Aseguró que el presidente ruso, Vladimir Putin, quería obligar a los residentes a huir de las principales ciudades de Ucrania. "Si nuestros puentes se derrumban, conseguiremos salir de esta situación, pero su pueblo también lo notará… Se trata de la máxima escalada de esta guerra", dijo Zelenski a los periodistas. Rusia lleva desde la semana pasada atacando los puentes de Kiev con el objetivo de cortar las conexiones entre las dos partes de la capital y las rutas logísticas entre el centro y el este de Ucrania. MERZ PIDE FIN DE UNA "GUERRA SIN SENTIDO" Zelenski dijo que el enviado estadounidense, Steve Witkoff, le había mandado un mensaje para instarle a reanudar las conversaciones trilaterales lo antes posible. Señaló que Ucrania estaba dispuesta a reunirse este mes y esperaba que Rusia se sumara, pero añadió que los aliados occidentales deben ejercer más presión sobre Moscú para poner fin a la guerra. Más temprano en el día, durante la visita a la Academia de Ciencias, gravemente dañada, Merz hizo un llamamiento a Putin para que "ponga fin a esta guerra sin sentido". "Estamos preparados para conversaciones, estamos preparados para debatir cómo poner fin a esta guerra, pero estos ataques bárbaros frente la población civil de Ucrania deben cesar", dijo el líder alemán. El Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores de Rusia dijo el sábado que Moscú seguiría atacando sistemáticamente objetivos en Ucrania en lo que calificó de ataques de represalia por los ataques ucranianos contra Rusia. Advirtió a los ciudadanos extranjeros y al personal diplomático que no viajaran a Ucrania. (1 dólar = 0,8887 euros)

item.title: Eagles RT Lane Johnson inactive vs. Rams
item.description: Philadelphia Eagles All-Pro right tackle Lane Johnson was listed as inactive for Sunday's game against the visiting Los Angeles Rams.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Philadelphia Eagles All-Pro right tackle Lane Johnson was listed as inactive for Sunday's game against the visiting Los Angeles Rams. Johnson was given a game designation as questionable earlier Sunday due to personal reasons before the Eagles ruled him out 90 minutes prior to kickoff. Philadelphia (2-1) is without six starters in all: Johnson, wide receiver DeVonta Smith, tight end Dallas Goedert, left guard Landon Dickerson, linebacker Zack Baun and safety Marcus Epps. Wideout Hollywood Brown, offensive tackle Fred Johnson and quarterback Cole Payton also were listed as inactive. Rookie tackle Markel Bell started in place of Johnson. Johnson, who turned 36 in May, told reporters in the summer that the 2026 season probably would be his last, citing priorities and his parents' health among his reasons. The two-time first-team All-Pro reportedly was mulling retirement following a 2025 campaign that saw him sit out the final seven games of the regular season and the team's NFC wild-card loss to the San Francisco 49ers due to a Lisfranc injury. Johnson is a two-time Super Bowl champion and six-time Pro Bowl selection. He has started all three games this season and 171 in his career since Philadelphia drafted him with the No. 4 overall pick in 2013. As for the Rams (1-2), star defensive end Aaron Donald joined tight end Colby Parkinson, cornerbacks Cam Lampkin and Jaylen Watson, offensive lineman Bill Murray, wide receiver C.J. Daniels and quarterback Ty Simpson (emergency third QB) as inactive for the contest. --Field Level Media

item.title: Britain's Green Party votes to class Zionism as a form of racism
item.description: Britain's Green Party voted on Sunday to class Zionism as a form of racism, drawing criticism from British Jews and from the Israeli government which said it now viewed the party as "a body that gives legitimacy to terrorism".
item.dc:creator: David Milliken
item.content:encoded: Britain's Green Party voted on Sunday to class Zionism as a form of racism, drawing criticism from British Jews and from the Israeli government which said it now viewed the party as "a body that gives legitimacy to terrorism". The party – which received 6% of the vote in national elections in 2024 – said it regarded Zionism as "an ethnonationalist political project" and repeated its call for Britain's Labour government to end all arms trade with Israel. "The motion also restates the Green Party's backing for the right to self-determination and calls for the establishment of a single democratic state throughout historic Palestine," the party said in a statement. The definition of Zionism – which inspired the foundation of the modern state of Israel in the 20th century – and what it implies for the rights of non-Jews in Israel and neighbouring territory, is contentious. Jewish groups sometimes define it as a right to Jewish self-determination. The Green Party motion passed by a majority of 1,022 to 813 despite opposition from many senior figures. Party leader Zack Polanski, who is seeking election to Parliament on Thursday in former Prime Minister Keir Starmer's now-vacant London constituency, did not vote. The result was condemned by British Jewish groups. "The Green Party has made antisemitism party policy and become a racist party," the Movement for Progressive Judaism said, adding that the support of some Jews for the motion did not mean it would not be used to discriminate against others. Israeli foreign minister Gideon Sa’ar has decided to declare Polanski barred from entering Israel, the foreign ministry said in a post on X Sunday. It said the Green Party motion "constitutes a clear antisemitic text according to the IHRA (International Holocaust Remembrance Alliance) definition, as it denies the Jewish people’s right to self-determination," the ministry said. Mothin Ali, deputy leader of the Green Party and a supporter of the motion, told Sky News on Saturday that the heavy Palestinian death toll in Israel's conflict with Hamas – which followed the Palestinian militant group's deadly 2023 attack on an Israeli music festival – was the key context for the vote. "The motion defines Zionism quite clearly. It defines it as an ethnonationalist movement. It defines it as ethnic cleansing. It defines it as genocide," Ali said. Britain's government views Israeli settlers' actions in the West Bank as [USN:L8N45007X TEXT:"amounting to ethnic cleansing"] but has said courts must decide if other Israeli actions qualify as genocide. Israel – which rejects claims of ethnic cleansing and genocide – called on Sunday for other British political parties to condemn the Green Party vote. "The Greens have adopted not only the green of Hamas, but also its ideology: the elimination of the State of Israel through armed struggle," it said. Polanski and other senior Green Party figures said they would "continue to call out the heinous crimes of the Netanyahu government," and that "there is no conflict between supporting the rights of Palestinians and the rights of Jewish people."

item.title: Iran's oil minister resigns for personal reasons, state media reports
item.description: Iran's Oil Minister Mohsen Paknejad has resigned for personal reasons, and Hamid Bovard, chief executive of the government-owned National Iranian Oil Company, will be acting minister, state media said on Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Iran's Oil Minister Mohsen Paknejad has resigned for personal reasons, and Hamid Bovard, chief executive of the government-owned National Iranian Oil Company, will be acting minister, state media said on Sunday. Mohsen Paknejad, oil minister of the OPEC member country since August 2024, resigned as the seven-month-old war between Iran and the US has [USN:L6N45K0UX TEXT:"put pressure"] on the country's economy. Mehdi Tabatabaei, communications deputy in the president's office, told state TV that Paknejad resigned for personal reasons "a long time ago" and his resignation was accepted by President Masoud Pezeshkian at Paknejad's insistence. "With acceptance of Mohsen Paknejad's resignation by Dr. Pezeshkian, Hamid Bovard has been appointed as acting oil minister", Tabatabaei said earlier on Sunday, according to state media. Before news of his resignation, Paknejad was quoted by state media as saying "revenues of the oil that we have sold are still coming and that will continue God willing".

item.title: Valentino unveils corset tops and chunky jewellery at fashion show in 19th-century Paris library
item.description: Valentino showed colourful corset tops, lace skirts and chunky gold necklaces on Sunday in a fashion show creative director Alessandro Michele dubbed "Antibiblioteca", set in the iconic reading room of the 19th-century Bibliothèque Sainte-Geneviève in Paris.
item.dc:creator: Helen Reid
item.content:encoded: Valentino showed colourful corset tops, lace skirts and chunky gold necklaces on Sunday in a fashion show creative director Alessandro Michele dubbed "Antibiblioteca", set in the iconic reading room of the 19th-century Bibliothèque Sainte-Geneviève in Paris. On a sun-drenched afternoon, celebrities arrived each clutching a book which they showed off to the cameras and a large crowd of assembled fans. Guests including actors Alexander Skarsgard and Cynthia Erivo, American stylist Law Roach, and Chinese model Yidan Huang took their seats at long oak reading tables dotted with green lamps, under the library's iron latticework ceiling arches. Michele has led the Roman [USN:L8N3YK19Q TEXT:"fashion house"] since March 2024 and is under pressure to revive sales at the brand that swung to a €103 million [USN:S8N40Y041 TEXT:"loss"] last year as revenues fell 15%. He was previously creative director at Gucci for eight years where his maximalist aesthetic and gender-fluid, eccentric designs like fur-lined loafers [USN:L8N32K398 TEXT:"reinvigorated"] the brand and boosted sales. Models prowled along the library stacks in tight silk corset tops in bright blue, yellow, or hot pink, paired with skirts in contrasting colours. Dresses were strapless too, with the final look a floor-length Valentino red number with a giant black bow. Lace skirts and shirts had ostrich-feather hems. Jewellery was chunky and colourful, with elaborate, baroque gold necklaces and giant pearl earrings. Women and men wore cross-body handbags or held rectangular clutches with studs and sequins. Men wore half-buttoned double-breasted jackets or sequinned shirts, sporting tinted sunglasses and bright baseball caps with "VILLAIN TEEN" printed on them. In June Valentino's shareholders — Qatar-backed Mayhoola, which owns 70% of the company, and French luxury group Kering, which holds the remaining 30% — committed additional financial support for 2026 after debt increased. Kering has options to increase its ownership to 100% before 2029.

item.title: Jonathan Taylor, Colts rush past injury-riddled Commanders
item.description: Jonathan Taylor ran for two touchdowns and the Indianapolis Colts pulled away in the fourth quarter to record a 30-13 victory over the undermanned Washington Commanders on Sunday in London.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Jonathan Taylor ran for two touchdowns and the Indianapolis Colts pulled away in the fourth quarter to record a 30-13 victory over the undermanned Washington Commanders on Sunday in London. Taylor scored on a pair of 5-yard runs, enabling Indianapolis (2-2) to overcome a quick 6-0 deficit. He finished with 95 yards on 20 carries as the Colts made the most of their 257 yards. Quarterback Daniel Jones shrugged off a pair of early turnovers to complete 19 of 34 passes for 143 yards and an interception. He also added the clinching score by running 5 yards on 3rd-and-2 for a touchdown with 11:38 left in the game that made it a two-touchdown margin. Washington (1-3) played most of the day with rookie Athan Kaliakmanis at quarterback after starter Marcus Mariota suffered a right knee injury in the first quarter and wasn't able to return. Kaliakmanis completed 15 of 33 passes for 186 yards with a touchdown and an interception. Mariota connected on 3 of 4 passes for 46 yards and rushed for 35 yards on one carry before departing. The Commanders got off to a quick start, getting a strip-sack on Indianapolis' second play and converting that into Drew Stevens' 31-yard field goal just 2:03 into the game. Stevens made it 6-0 on a 29-yard field goal from Stevens with 6:21 left in the quarter. That lead held until the Colts, who managed only 33 yards on their first four possessions, finally found traction. Taylor's first touchdown run with 3:23 remaining in the half put them ahead for good and Spencer Shrader's 48-yard field goal made it 10-6 at the break. Taylor scored again at the 12:45 mark of the third quarter, four plays after Kaliakmanis tossed an interception. But Kaliakmanis responded with a 47-yard touchdown pass to Traylon Burks with 10:39 left in the period. Shrader drilled a 52-yarder with 7:03 remaining in the third for a 20-13 advantage. In the fourth quarter, he added a 44-yarder with 5:48 on the clock to cap the scoring. --Field Level Media

item.title: Vídeo de porta-aviões dos EUA no Rio de Janeiro não foi feito em meio às eleições
item.description: Imagens de um porta-aviões dos Estados Unidos no Rio de Janeiro não foram feitas no contexto das eleições brasileiras deste domingo, como afirmam publicações nas redes sociais. A gravação circula ao menos desde maio deste ano.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: Imagens de um porta-aviões dos Estados Unidos no Rio de Janeiro não foram feitas no contexto das eleições brasileiras deste domingo, como afirmam publicações nas redes sociais. A gravação circula ao menos desde maio deste ano. Estes são os principais detalhes: “Porta-avião americano chega ao Rio de Janeiro”, dizem postagens com o registro no Instagram. “Bora tudo de novo… Somente em caso de guerra ou conflito instalado as embaixadas fecham”, descreve a legenda de uma delas. Na última sexta-feira, a embaixada dos EUA no Brasil anunciou a suspensão dos serviços consulares no país citando preocupações com segurança. A medida ocorreu em meio ao temor de autoridades brasileiras de que o governo do presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, tente interferir nas eleições. O vídeo checado, no entanto, não tem relação com esses fatos -- um perfil no Instagram compartilhou as mesmas imagens em 10 de maio deste ano. No registro, um homem mostra a embarcação e diz: “O porta-avião que acabou de chegar, americano, aqui na Baía de Guanabara”. Ele filma a ponte Rio-Niterói e o nome do navio, Nimitz . O porta-aviões USS Nimitz esteve na capital fluminense em maio para um exercício conjunto, segundo a embaixada dos EUA no Brasil e as forças militares dos dois países. Segundo a Marinha brasileira, a embarcação deixou a cidade ainda naquele mês . Desde então, não há registros de que o navio tenha voltado ao Brasil. Veredicto: Legenda errada. O vídeo de um porta-aviões dos EUA no Rio de Janeiro é de maio e não está relacionado às eleições brasileiras. Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check.
